title: How to Access NotebookLM Via API?
snippet: The NotebookLM API requires Google Cloud’s NotebookLM Enterprise product which requires identity/auth setup and buying a subscription which contains at least 15 licenses and can contain up to 5,000 licenses. (More rules about regions.)

title: Create and manage notebooks (API)
snippet:
- [Set up Gemini Notebook Enterprise](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/set-up-notebooklm).
- [Get licenses for Gemini Notebook Enterprise](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/set-up-licensing) and assign a license to your user account.
- [Grant the Cloud NotebookLM User role](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/set-up-notebooklm#grant-roles) (`roles/discoveryengine.notebookLmUser`) to your user account.
- In a local terminal or [Cloud Shell](https://docs.cloud.google.com/shell/docs), sign in to the [Google Cloud CLI](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install-sdk) with your user credentials by running the [`gcloud auth login`](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/auth/login) command:
```
gcloud auth login
```
Signing in with your user credentials ensures that `gcloud auth print-access-token` generates an access token for your user account. The [`projects.locations.notebooks` REST API](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/reference/rest/v1alpha/projects.locations.notebooks) methods on this page require an authenticated user account with an active Gemini Notebook Enterprise license.

title: Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM) API: Key and Pricing
snippet:
No, not for personal accounts. Google’s only documented Gemini Notebook API belongs to Gemini Notebook Enterprise on Google Cloud, and its setup steps require Enterprise licenses before you make a single call ([Google Cloud](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/api-notebooks), 2026). Free, Plus, Pro and Ultra accounts have nothing official to call. As a result, every consumer integration you’ll find works around the app, not through it. In fact, a public request for an official, OAuth-based NotebookLM MCP server is open on Google’s MCP repository ([GitHub](https://github.com/google/mcp/issues/19), 2026). Its author argued that an official server would bring the “stability and security required for professional workflows”. Why does that matter to you? Workarounds can break whenever Google changes the web app, so anything you build on one needs a plan for the day it stops.

`https://mcp.kortex-notebooklm.com/mcp` as a Streamable HTTP server, then sign in on the Kortex consent page it opens.

title: Set up Gemini Notebook Enterprise
snippet:
To complete the setup, you must have your organization's identity provider (IdP) configured in Google Cloud. Correct setup for identity is important for two reasons:
- It lets your users use their current corporate credentials to access the Gemini Notebook Enterprise user interface.
- It ensures that users see only the notebooks which they own or which have been shared with them.

- Workforce Identity Federation: If you use an external identity provider (Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Ping, PingFederate, or another OIDC or SAML 2.0 IdP), but don't want to sync your identities into Cloud Identity, then you must set up [Workforce Identity Federation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workforce-identity-federation) in Google Cloud before you can turn on data source access control for Gemini Notebook Enterprise.

As the project owner, you need to assign the Cloud NotebookLM Admin role to any users who you want to be able to administer Gemini Notebook Enterprise in this project:
1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the **IAM** page.
[Go to IAM](https://console.cloud.google.com/projectselector/iam-admin/iam?supportedpurview=)
2. Select the project.
3. Click **Grant access**.
4. In the **New principals** field, enter the user identifier. This is typically the email address for a Google Account or a user group.
5. In the **Select a role** list, select **Cloud NotebookLM Admin**. For more information, see [User roles](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/overview#user_roles).
6. Click **Save**.

title: Does NotebookLM have an API? The 2026 answer
snippet:
Yes and no, and the honest answer changed during 2026. Google does publish an API for Gemini Notebook Enterprise, in preview, behind a Cloud project and a licence. The consumer NotebookLM you log into with a personal Google account still has no developer key, and the standalone Podcast API that some posts point at is deprecated and not taking new customers.
Most answers you will find say flatly "there is no API". That was true and is now wrong, which is worse than either.
Google documents a REST surface for Gemini Notebook Enterprise, including notebook operations and audio overviews — a notebook holds one audio overview at a time, created through `notebooks.audioOverviews.create`. It is marked pre-GA, which means the terms and the shape can both move.
The access path is the part people miss. It needs a Google Cloud project and a Gemini Enterprise or Education Premium licence, set up by an administrator. It is not a key you sign up for on a developer console, and it does not reach the notebooks in your personal account.
Deprecated. Google is not allowlisting new customers for it. If a tutorial tells you to request access, that tutorial is out of date.
Community projects that drive the same interfaces the web app uses. There are several, in Python and in Node, exposing them as a CLI, as an MCP server, or as a local REST API. They work, they are fast, and they reach your own notebooks with your own login.

Three questions settle it.
**Do you have an enterprise licence and an administrator?** Then use the official API. It is supported, it is the only route with a contract behind it, and nothing below competes with that.
**Do you need your own personal notebooks?** Then the official API is out, and a community tool is the only route that exists.
**Do you need it to keep working unattended?** Weigh how quickly the project you pick has recovered from past breakages. That is the only signal that matters, and the commit history tells you more than the README.
- When the work is contractual — a client deliverable, a regulated pipeline, an SLA. An undocumented interface has no promise attached to it.
- When you only need text generation over documents. The Gemini API is public, supported and cheaper to reason about; NotebookLM's value is its grounding and citation behaviour, not its text generation.
- When you cannot run a browser anywhere. Login still happens in a real Chrome, once, even for the tools that avoid the browser afterwards.

- **Does NotebookLM have an API?** Yes, through the useapi.net NotebookLM API (Gemini Notebook API), a third-party REST API that drives your own Google account, so it works on free and paid consumer plans and covers everything in the web app: chat with citations, Deep Research and every Studio output.
